activate_all_roles_on_login.desc: Automatically set all granted roles as active after the user has authenticated successfully.

admin_address.desc: IP address to bind to for service connection. Address can be an IPv4 address, IPv6 address, or host name. Wildcard values *, ::, 0.0.0.0 are not allowed. Address value can have following optional network namespace separated by the delimiter / from the address value. E.g., the following value 192.168.1.1/red specifies IP addresses to listen for incoming TCP connections that have to be placed into the namespace 'red'. Using of network namespace requires its support from underlying Operating System. Attempt to specify a network namespace for a platform that doesn't support it results in error during socket creation.

admin_port.desc: Port number to use for service connection, built-in default (33062)

admin_ssl_ca.desc: CA file in PEM format (check OpenSSL docs) for --admin-port

admin_ssl_cert.desc: X509 cert in PEM format for --admin-port

admin_ssl_crl.desc: CRL file in PEM format (check OpenSSL docs) for --admin-port

admin_ssl_key.desc: X509 key in PEM format for --admin-port

admin_tls_ciphersuites.desc: TLS v1.3 ciphersuite to use for --admin-port

admin_tls_version.desc: TLS version for --admin-port, permitted values are TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3

allow_suspicious_udfs.desc: Allows use of UDFs consisting of only one symbol xxx() without corresponding xxx_init() or xxx_deinit(). That also means that one can load any function from any library, for example exit() from libc.so

archive.desc: Enable or disable ARCHIVE plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

authentication_policy.desc: Defines policies around how user account can be configured with Multi Factor authentication methods during CREATE/ALTER USER statement. This variable accepts at-most 3 comma separated list of authentication factor descriptions. Allowed factor descriptions are: (empty) - factor is optional, any authentication method is allowed. * - factor is mandatory, any authentication method is allowed. <plugin> - <plugin> is mandatory authentication method. *:<plugin> - factor is mandatory, <plugin> is default authentication method. The first factor cannot be optional and if neither mandatory nor default method is specified, caching_sha2_password is assumed as default.

auto_generate_certs.desc: Auto generate SSL certificates at server startup if none of the other SSL system variables are specified and certificate/key files are not present in data directory. (Defaults to on; use --skip-auto-generate-certs to disable.)

auto_increment_increment.desc: Auto-increment columns are incremented by this

auto_increment_offset.desc: Offset added to Auto-increment columns. Used when auto-increment-increment != 1

autocommit.desc: Set default value for autocommit (0 or 1) (Defaults to on; use --skip-autocommit to disable.)

automatic_sp_privileges.desc: Creating and dropping stored procedures alters ACLs (Defaults to on; use --skip-automatic-sp-privileges to disable.)

back_log.desc: The number of outstanding connection requests MySQL can have. This comes into play when the main MySQL thread gets very many connection requests in a very short time

basedir.desc: Path to installation directory. All paths are usually resolved relative to this

big_tables.desc: Allow big result sets by saving all temporary sets on file (Solves most 'table full' errors)

bind_address.desc: IP address(es) to bind to. Syntax: address[,address]..., where address can be an IPv4 address, IPv6 address, host name or one of the wildcard values *, ::, 0.0.0.0. In case more than one address is specified in a comma-separated list, wildcard values are not allowed. Every address can have optional network namespace separated by the delimiter / from the address value. E.g., the following value 192.168.1.1/red,172.16.1.1/green,193.168.1.1 specifies three IP addresses to listen for incoming TCP connections two of that have to be placed in corresponding namespaces: the address 192.168.1.1 must be placed into the namespace red and the address 172.16.1.1 must be placed into the namespace green. Using of network namespace requires its support from underlying Operating System. Attempt to specify a network namespace for a platform that doesn't support it results in error during socket creation.

binlog_cache_size.desc: The size of the transactional cache for updates to transactional engines for the binary log. If you often use transactions containing many statements, you can increase this to get more performance

binlog_checksum.desc: Type of BINLOG_CHECKSUM_ALG. Include checksum for log events in the binary log. Possible values are NONE and CRC32; default is CRC32.

binlog_direct_non_transactional_updates.desc: Causes updates to non-transactional engines using statement format to be written directly to binary log, after executing them and before committing the transaction. Before using this option make sure that there are no dependencies between transactional and non-transactional tables such as in the statement INSERT INTO t_myisam SELECT * FROM t_innodb; otherwise, replicas may diverge.

binlog_encryption.desc: Enable/disable binary and relay logs encryption.

binlog_error_action.desc: When statements cannot be written to the binary log due to a fatal error, this option determines whether the server ignores the error and closes the binary log, or aborts.

binlog_expire_logs_auto_purge.desc: Controls whether the server shall automatically purge binary log files or not. If this variable is set to FALSE then the server will not purge binary log files automatically. (Defaults to on; use --skip-binlog-expire-logs-auto-purge to disable.)

binlog_expire_logs_seconds.desc: If non-zero, binary logs will be purged after binlog_expire_logs_seconds seconds; Purges happen at startup and at binary log rotation.

binlog_format.deprecated: '@@binlog_format' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
binlog_format.desc: The format used when writing the binary log. ROW writes each changed row in a binary format. STATEMENT writes SQL statements. MIXED writes SQL statements for most statements, and row format for statements that cannot be replayed in a deterministic manner using SQL. If NDBCLUSTER is enabled and binlog-format is MIXED, the format switches to row-based and back implicitly for each query accessing an NDBCLUSTER table. This option is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

binlog_group_commit_sync_delay.desc: The number of microseconds the server waits for the binary log group commit sync queue to fill before continuing. Default: 0. Min: 0. Max: 1000000.

binlog_group_commit_sync_no_delay_count.desc: If there are this many transactions in the commit sync queue and the server is waiting for more transactions to be enqueued (as set using --binlog-group-commit-sync-delay), the commit procedure resumes.

binlog_gtid_simple_recovery.desc: If this option is enabled, the server does not open more than two binary logs when initializing GTID_PURGED and GTID_EXECUTED, either during server restart or when binary logs are being purged. Enabling this option is useful when the server has already generated many binary logs without GTID events (e.g., having GTID_MODE = OFF). Note: If this option is enabled, GLOBAL.GTID_EXECUTED and GLOBAL.GTID_PURGED may be initialized wrongly in two cases: (1) All binary logs were generated by MySQL 5.7.5 or older, and GTID_MODE was ON for some binary logs but OFF for the newest binary log. (2) The oldest existing binary log was generated by MySQL 5.7.5 or older, and SET GTID_PURGED was issued after the oldest binary log was generated. If a wrong set is computed in one of case (1) or case (2), it will remain wrong even if the server is later restarted with this option disabled. (Defaults to on; use --skip-binlog-gtid-simple-recovery to disable.)

binlog_max_flush_queue_time.deprecated: '@@binlog_max_flush_queue_time' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
binlog_max_flush_queue_time.desc: The maximum time that the binary log group commit will keep reading transactions before it flush the transactions to the binary log (and optionally sync, depending on the value of sync_binlog).

binlog_order_commits.desc: Issue internal commit calls in the same order as transactions are written to the binary log. Default is to order commits. (Defaults to on; use --skip-binlog-order-commits to disable.)

binlog_rotate_encryption_master_key_at_s.desc: Force binlog encryption master key rotation at startup

binlog_row_event_max_size.desc: The maximum size of a row-based binary log event in bytes. Rows will be grouped into events smaller than this size if possible. The value has to be a multiple of 256.

binlog_row_image.desc: Controls whether rows should be logged in 'FULL', 'NOBLOB' or 'MINIMAL' formats. 'FULL', means that all columns in the before and after image are logged. 'NOBLOB', means that mysqld avoids logging blob columns whenever possible (e.g. blob column was not changed or is not part of primary key). 'MINIMAL', means that a PK equivalent (PK columns or full row if there is no PK in the table) is logged in the before image, and only changed columns are logged in the after image. (Default: FULL).

binlog_row_metadata.desc: Controls how much type information is written to the binary log when using ROW format. FULL causes all metadata to be logged. MINIMAL means that only metadata actually needed by replicas is logged.

binlog_row_value_options.desc: When set to PARTIAL_JSON, this option enables a space-efficient row-based binary log format for UPDATE statements that modify a JSON value using only the functions JSON_SET, JSON_REPLACE, and JSON_REMOVE. For such updates, only the modified parts of the JSON document are included in the binary log, so small changes of big documents may need significantly less space.

binlog_rows_query_log_events.desc: Allow writing of Rows_query_log events into binary log.

binlog_stmt_cache_size.desc: The size of the statement cache for updates to non-transactional engines for the binary log. If you often use statements updating a great number of rows, you can increase this to get more performance

binlog_transaction_compression.desc: Whether to compress transactions or not. Transactions are compressed using the ZSTD compression algorythm.

binlog_transaction_compression_level_zst.desc: Specifies the transaction compression level for ZSTD transaction compression in the binary log.

binlog_transaction_dependency_history_si.desc: Maximum number of rows to keep in the writeset history.

blackhole.desc: Enable or disable BLACKHOLE plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

bulk_insert_buffer_size.desc: Size of tree cache used in bulk insert optimisation. Note that this is a limit per thread!

caching_sha2_password_auto_generate_rsa_.desc: Auto generate RSA keys at server startup if corresponding system variables are not specified and key files are not present at the default location. (Defaults to on; use --skip-caching-sha2-password-auto-generate-rsa-keys to disable.)

caching_sha2_password_digest_rounds.desc: Number of SHA2 rounds to be done when storing a password hash onto disk.

caching_sha2_password_private_key_path.desc: A fully qualified path to the private RSA key used for authentication.

caching_sha2_password_public_key_path.desc: A fully qualified path to the public RSA key used for authentication.

check_proxy_users.desc: If set to FALSE (the default), then proxy user identity will not be mapped for authentication plugins which support mapping from grant tables.  When set to TRUE, users associated with authentication plugins which signal proxy user mapping should be done according to GRANT PROXY privilege definition.

check_table_functions.desc: On upgrade, the server attempts to open tables with SQL functions in their DEFAULT, INDEX, and PARTITION clauses, virtual columns, and CONSTRAINTs. WARN runs the test but proceeds even if potential issues are found; ABORT (default) stops the server if potential issues are found.

completion_type.desc: The transaction completion type, one of NO_CHAIN, CHAIN, RELEASE

concurrent_insert.desc: Use concurrent insert with MyISAM. Possible values are NEVER, AUTO, ALWAYS

connect_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the mysqld server is waiting for a connect packet before responding with 'Bad handshake'

connection_memory_chunk_size.desc: Chunk size regulating frequency of updating the global memory counter

connection_memory_limit.desc: Maximum amount of memory connection can consume

console.desc: Write error output on screen; don't remove the console window on windows.

create_admin_listener_thread.desc: Use a dedicated thread for listening incoming connections on admin interface

cte_max_recursion_depth.desc: Abort a recursive common table expression if it does more than this number of iterations.

datadir.desc: Path to the database root directory

default_password_lifetime.desc: The number of days after which the password will expire.

default_storage_engine.desc: The default storage engine for new tables

default_table_encryption.desc: Database and tablespace are created with this default encryption property unless the user specifies an explicit encryption property.

default_tmp_storage_engine.desc: The default storage engine for new explicit temporary tables

default_week_format.desc: The default week format used by WEEK() functions

delayed_insert_limit.deprecated: '@@delayed_insert_limit' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
delayed_insert_limit.desc: After inserting delayed_insert_limit rows, the INSERT DELAYED handler will check if there are any SELECT statements pending. If so, it allows these to execute before continuing. This variable is deprecated along with INSERT DELAYED.

delayed_insert_timeout.deprecated: '@@delayed_insert_timeout' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
delayed_insert_timeout.desc: How long a INSERT DELAYED thread should wait for INSERT statements before terminating. This variable is deprecated along with INSERT DELAYED.

delayed_queue_size.deprecated: '@@delayed_queue_size' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
delayed_queue_size.desc: What size queue (in rows) should be allocated for handling INSERT DELAYED. If the queue becomes full, any client that does INSERT DELAYED will wait until there is room in the queue again. This variable is deprecated along with INSERT DELAYED.

disabled_storage_engines.desc: Limit CREATE TABLE for the storage engines listed

disconnect_on_expired_password.desc: Give clients that don't signal password expiration support execution time error(s) instead of connection error (Defaults to on; use --skip-disconnect-on-expired-password to disable.)

div_precision_increment.desc: Precision of the result of '/' operator will be increased on that value

end_markers_in_json.desc: In JSON output ("EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON" and optimizer trace), if variable is set to 1, repeats the structure's key (if it has one) near the closing bracket

enforce_gtid_consistency.desc: Prevents execution of statements that would be impossible to log in a transactionally safe manner. Currently, the disallowed statements include CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE inside transactions, all updates to non-transactional tables, and CREATE TABLE ... SELECT.

eq_range_index_dive_limit.desc: The optimizer will use existing index statistics instead of doing index dives for equality ranges if the number of equality ranges for the index is larger than or equal to this number. If set to 0, index dives are always used.

event_scheduler.desc: Enable the event scheduler. Possible values are ON, OFF, and DISABLED (keep the event scheduler completely deactivated, it cannot be activated run-time)

explain_format.desc: The default format in which the EXPLAIN statement displays information. Valid values are TRADITIONAL (default), TREE, JSON and TRADITIONAL_STRICT. TRADITIONAL_STRICT is only used internally by the mtr test suite, and is not meant to be used anywhere else.

explain_json_format_version.desc: The JSON format version for EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON queries with the old (non-hypergraph) join optimizer. Valid values are 1 and 2.

explicit_defaults_for_timestamp.deprecated: Marked deprecated in the server option help text.
explicit_defaults_for_timestamp.desc: This option causes CREATE TABLE to create all TIMESTAMP columns as NULL with DEFAULT NULL attribute, Without this option, TIMESTAMP columns are NOT NULL and have implicit DEFAULT clauses. The old behavior is deprecated. The variable can only be set by users having the SUPER privilege. (Defaults to on; use --skip-explicit-defaults-for-timestamp to disable.)

external_locking.desc: Use system (external) locking (disabled by default). With this option enabled you can run myisamchk to test (not repair) tables while the MySQL server is running. Disable with --skip-external-locking.

federated.desc: Enable or disable FEDERATED plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

flush.desc: Flush MyISAM tables to disk between SQL commands

flush_time.desc: A dedicated thread is created to flush all tables at the given interval

ft_boolean_syntax.desc: List of operators for MATCH ... AGAINST ( ... IN BOOLEAN MODE)

ft_max_word_len.desc: The maximum length of the word to be included in a FULLTEXT index. Note: FULLTEXT indexes must be rebuilt after changing this variable

ft_min_word_len.desc: The minimum length of the word to be included in a FULLTEXT index. Note: FULLTEXT indexes must be rebuilt after changing this variable

ft_query_expansion_limit.desc: Number of best matches to use for query expansion

ft_stopword_file.desc: Use stopwords from this file instead of built-in list

gdb.desc: Set up signals usable for debugging.

general_log.desc: Log connections and queries to a table or log file. Defaults to logging to a file hostname.log, or if --log-output=TABLE is used, to a table mysql.general_log.

general_log_file.desc: Log connections and queries to given file

generated_random_password_length.desc: Determines the length randomly generated passwords in CREATE USER-,SET PASSWORD- or ALTER USER statements

global_connection_memory_limit.desc: Maximum amount of memory all connections can consume

global_connection_memory_tracking.desc: Enable updating the global memory counter and checking the global connection memory limit exceeding

group_concat_max_len.desc: The maximum length of the result of function GROUP_CONCAT()

group_replication_consistency.desc: Transaction consistency guarantee, possible values: EVENTUAL, BEFORE_ON_PRIMARY_FAILOVER, BEFORE, AFTER, BEFORE_AND_AFTER

gtid_executed_compression_period.desc: Compress the mysql.gtid_executed table whenever this number of transactions have been added, by waking up a foreground thread (compress_gtid_table). This compression method only operates when binary logging is disabled on the replica; if binary logging is enabled, the table is compressed every time the binary log is rotated, and this value is ignored. Before MySQL 8.0.23, the default is 1000, and from MySQL 8.0.23, the default is zero, which disables this compression method. This is because in releases from MySQL 8.0.17, InnoDB transactions are written to the mysql.gtid_executed table by a separate process to non-InnoDB transactions. If the server has a mix of InnoDB and non-InnoDB transactions, attempting to compress the table with the compress_gtid_table thread can slow this process, so from MySQL 8.0.17 it is recommended that you set gtid_executed_compression_period to 0.

gtid_mode.desc: Controls whether Global Transaction Identifiers (GTIDs) are enabled. Can be OFF, OFF_PERMISSIVE, ON_PERMISSIVE, or ON. OFF means that no transaction has a GTID. OFF_PERMISSIVE means that new transactions (committed in a client session using GTID_NEXT='AUTOMATIC') are not assigned any GTID, and replicated transactions are allowed to have or not have a GTID. ON_PERMISSIVE means that new transactions are assigned a GTID, and replicated transactions are allowed to have or not have a GTID. ON means that all transactions have a GTID. ON is required on a source before any replica can use SOURCE_AUTO_POSITION=1. To safely switch from OFF to ON, first set all servers to OFF_PERMISSIVE, then set all servers to ON_PERMISSIVE, then wait for all transactions without a GTID to be replicated and executed on all servers, and finally set all servers to GTID_MODE = ON.

have_profiling.deprecated: '@@have_profiling' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

have_query_cache.deprecated: '@@have_query_cache' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

histogram_generation_max_mem_size.desc: Maximum amount of memory available for generating histograms

host_cache_size.desc: How many host names should be cached to avoid resolving.

information_schema_stats_expiry.desc: The number of seconds after which mysqld server will fetch data from storage engine and replace the data in cache.

init_connect.desc: Command(s) that are executed for each new connection

init_file.desc: Read SQL commands from this file at startup

init_replica.desc: Command(s) that are executed by the replication applier thread each time the applier threads start.

init_slave.deprecated: '@@init_slave' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please use init_replica instead.
init_slave.desc: This option is deprecated. Use init_replica instead.

initialize.desc: Create the default database and exit. Create a super user with a random expired password and store it into the log.

initialize_insecure.desc: Create the default database and exit. Create a super user with empty password.

innodb_adaptive_flushing.desc: Attempt flushing dirty pages to avoid IO bursts at checkpoints. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-adaptive-flushing to disable.)

innodb_adaptive_flushing_lwm.desc: Percentage of log capacity below which no adaptive flushing happens.

innodb_adaptive_hash_index.desc: Enable InnoDB adaptive hash index (enabled by default). Disable with --skip-innodb-adaptive-hash-index.

innodb_adaptive_hash_index_parts.desc: Number of InnoDB Adaptive Hash Index Partitions. (default = 8).

innodb_adaptive_max_sleep_delay.desc: The upper limit of the sleep delay in usec. Value of 0 disables it.

innodb_api_disable_rowlock.desc: Disable row lock when direct access InnoDB through InnoDB APIs

innodb_api_enable_binlog.desc: Enable binlog for applications direct access InnoDB through InnoDB APIs

innodb_api_enable_mdl.desc: Enable MDL for applications direct access InnoDB through InnoDB APIs

innodb_autoextend_increment.desc: Data file autoextend increment in megabytes

innodb_autoinc_lock_mode.desc: The AUTOINC lock modes supported by InnoDB: 0 => Old style AUTOINC locking (for backward compatibility); 1 => New style AUTOINC locking; 2 => No AUTOINC locking (unsafe for SBR)

innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size.desc: Size of a single memory chunk within each buffer pool instance for resizing buffer pool. Online buffer pool resizing happens at this granularity.

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_at_shutdown.desc: Dump the buffer pool into a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-buffer-pool-dump-at-shutdown to disable.)

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_now.desc: Trigger an immediate dump of the buffer pool into a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

innodb_buffer_pool_dump_pct.desc: Dump only the hottest N% of each buffer pool, defaults to 25

innodb_buffer_pool_filename.desc: Filename to/from which to dump/load the InnoDB buffer pool

innodb_buffer_pool_in_core_file.desc: This option has no effect if @@core_file is OFF. If @@core_file is ON, and this option is OFF, then the core dump file will be generated only if it is possible to exclude buffer pool from it. As soon as it will be determined that such exclusion is impossible a warning will be emitted and @@core_file will be set to OFF to prevent generating a core dump. If this option is enabled then core dumping logic will not be affected. This option is disabled by default if the platforms supports MADV_DONTDUMP, otherwise it is enabled by default.

innodb_buffer_pool_instances.desc: Number of buffer pool instances, set to higher value on high-end machines to increase scalability

innodb_buffer_pool_load_abort.desc: Abort a currently running load of the buffer pool

innodb_buffer_pool_load_at_startup.desc: Load the buffer pool from a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-buffer-pool-load-at-startup to disable.)

innodb_buffer_pool_load_now.desc: Trigger an immediate load of the buffer pool from a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

innodb_buffer_pool_size.desc: The size of the memory buffer InnoDB uses to cache data and indexes of its tables.

innodb_change_buffer_max_size.desc: Maximum on-disk size of change buffer in terms of percentage of the buffer pool.

innodb_change_buffering.desc: Buffer changes to reduce random access: OFF (default), ON, inserting, deleting, changing, or purging.

innodb_checksum_algorithm.desc: The algorithm InnoDB uses for page checksumming. Possible values are CRC32 (hardware accelerated if the CPU supports it) write crc32, allow any of the other checksums to match when reading; STRICT_CRC32 write crc32, do not allow other algorithms to match when reading; INNODB write a software calculated checksum, allow any other checksums to match when reading; STRICT_INNODB write a software calculated checksum, do not allow other algorithms to match when reading; NONE write a constant magic number, do not do any checksum verification when reading; STRICT_NONE write a constant magic number, do not allow values other than that magic number when reading; Files updated when this option is set to crc32 or strict_crc32 will not be readable by MySQL versions older than 5.6.3

innodb_cmp_per_index_enabled.desc: Enable INFORMATION_SCHEMA.innodb_cmp_per_index, may have negative impact on performance (off by default)

innodb_commit_concurrency.desc: Helps in performance tuning in heavily concurrent environments.

innodb_compression_failure_threshold_pct.desc: If the compression failure rate of a table is greater than this number more padding is added to the pages to reduce the failures. A value of zero implies no padding

innodb_compression_level.desc: Compression level used for compressed row format.  0 is no compression, 1 is fastest, 9 is best compression and default is 6.

innodb_compression_pad_pct_max.desc: Percentage of empty space on a data page that can be reserved to make the page compressible.

innodb_concurrency_tickets.desc: Number of times a thread is allowed to enter InnoDB within the same SQL query after it has once got the ticket

innodb_data_file_path.desc: Path to individual files and their sizes.

innodb_data_home_dir.desc: The common part for InnoDB table spaces.

innodb_ddl_buffer_size.desc: Maximum size of memory to use (in bytes) for DDL.

innodb_ddl_threads.desc: Maximum number of threads to use for  DDL.

innodb_deadlock_detect.desc: Enable/disable InnoDB deadlock detector (default ON). if set to OFF, deadlock detection is skipped, and we rely on innodb_lock_wait_timeout in case of deadlock. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-deadlock-detect to disable.)

innodb_dedicated_server.desc: Automatically scale innodb_buffer_pool_size and innodb_redo_log_capacity based on system memory.

innodb_default_row_format.desc: The default ROW FORMAT for all innodb tables created without explicit ROW_FORMAT. Possible values are REDUNDANT, COMPACT, and DYNAMIC. The ROW_FORMAT value COMPRESSED is not allowed

innodb_directories.desc: List of directories 'dir1;dir2;..;dirN' to scan for tablespace files. Default is to scan 'innodb-data-home-dir;innodb-undo-directory;datadir'

innodb_disable_sort_file_cache.desc: Whether to disable OS system file cache for sort I/O

innodb_doublewrite.desc: Enable InnoDB doublewrite buffer (enabled by default). Disable with --skip-innodb-doublewrite.

innodb_doublewrite_batch_size.desc: Number of double write pages to write in a batch

innodb_doublewrite_dir.desc: Use a separate directory for the doublewrite buffer files,

innodb_doublewrite_pages.desc: Number of double write pages per thread

innodb_extend_and_initialize.desc: Initialize the allocated space by writing zeros (enabled by default). (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-extend-and-initialize to disable.)

innodb_fast_shutdown.desc: Speeds up the shutdown process of the InnoDB storage engine. Possible values are 0, 1 (faster) or 2 (fastest - crash-like).

innodb_file_per_table.desc: Stores each InnoDB table to an .ibd file in the database dir. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-file-per-table to disable.)

innodb_fill_factor.desc: Percentage of B-tree page filled during bulk insert

innodb_flush_log_at_timeout.desc: Write and flush logs every (n) second.

innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit.desc: Set to 0 (write and flush once per second), 1 (write and flush at each commit), or 2 (write at commit, flush once per second).

innodb_flush_method.desc: With which method to flush data

innodb_flush_neighbors.desc: Set to 0 (don't flush neighbors from buffer pool), 1 (flush contiguous neighbors from buffer pool) or 2 (flush neighbors from buffer pool), when flushing a block

innodb_flush_sync.desc: Allow IO bursts at the checkpoints ignoring io_capacity setting. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-flush-sync to disable.)

innodb_flushing_avg_loops.desc: Number of iterations over which the background flushing is averaged.

innodb_force_load_corrupted.desc: Force InnoDB to load metadata of corrupted table.

innodb_force_recovery.desc: Helps to save your data in case the disk image of the database becomes corrupt.

innodb_fsync_threshold.desc: The value of this variable determines how often InnoDB calls fsync when creating a new file. Default is zero which would make InnoDB flush the entire file at once before closing it.

innodb_ft_aux_table.desc: FTS internal auxiliary table to be checked

innodb_ft_cache_size.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search cache size in bytes

innodb_ft_enable_diag_print.desc: Whether to enable additional FTS diagnostic printout

innodb_ft_enable_stopword.desc: Create FTS index with stopword. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-ft-enable-stopword to disable.)

innodb_ft_max_token_size.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search maximum token size in characters

innodb_ft_min_token_size.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search minimum token size in characters

innodb_ft_num_word_optimize.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search number of words to optimize for each optimize table call

innodb_ft_result_cache_limit.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search query result cache limit in bytes

innodb_ft_server_stopword_table.desc: The user supplied stopword table name.

innodb_ft_sort_pll_degree.desc: InnoDB Fulltext search parallel sort degree, will round up to nearest power of 2 number

innodb_ft_total_cache_size.desc: Total memory allocated for InnoDB Fulltext Search cache

innodb_ft_user_stopword_table.desc: User supplied stopword table name, effective in the session level.

innodb_idle_flush_pct.desc: Up to what percentage of dirty pages to be flushed when server is found idle.

innodb_io_capacity.desc: Number of IOPs the server can do. Tunes the background IO rate

innodb_io_capacity_max.desc: Limit to which innodb_io_capacity can be inflated.

innodb_lock_wait_timeout.desc: Timeout in seconds an InnoDB transaction may wait for a lock before being rolled back. Values above 100000000 disable the timeout.

innodb_log_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer which InnoDB uses to write log to the log files on disk.

innodb_log_checksums.desc: Whether to compute and require checksums for InnoDB redo log blocks (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-log-checksums to disable.)

innodb_log_compressed_pages.desc: Enables/disables the logging of entire compressed page images. InnoDB logs the compressed pages to prevent corruption if the zlib compression algorithm changes. When turned OFF, InnoDB will assume that the zlib compression algorithm doesn't change. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-log-compressed-pages to disable.)

innodb_log_file_size.deprecated: Marked deprecated in the server option help text.
innodb_log_file_size.desc: Size of each log file before upgrading to 8.0.30. Deprecated.

innodb_log_files_in_group.deprecated: Marked deprecated in the server option help text.
innodb_log_files_in_group.desc: Number of log files before upgrading to 8.0.30. Deprecated.

innodb_log_spin_cpu_abs_lwm.desc: Minimum value of cpu time for which spin-delay is used. Expressed in percentage of single cpu core.

innodb_log_spin_cpu_pct_hwm.desc: Maximum value of cpu time for which spin-delay is used. Expressed in percentage of all cpu cores.

innodb_log_wait_for_flush_spin_hwm.desc: Maximum value of average log flush time for which spin-delay is used. When flushing takes longer, user threads no longer spin when waiting forflushed redo. Expressed in microseconds.

innodb_log_write_ahead_size.desc: Log write ahead unit size to avoid read-on-write, it should match the OS cache block IO size.

innodb_log_writer_threads.desc: Whether the log writer threads should be activated (ON), or write/flush of the redo log should be done by each thread individually (OFF). (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-log-writer-threads to disable.)

innodb_lru_scan_depth.desc: How deep to scan LRU to keep it clean

innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct.desc: Percentage of dirty pages allowed in bufferpool.

innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct_lwm.desc: Percentage of dirty pages at which flushing kicks in.

innodb_max_purge_lag.desc: Desired maximum length of the purge queue (0 = no limit)

innodb_max_purge_lag_delay.desc: Maximum delay of user threads in micro-seconds

innodb_max_undo_log_size.desc: Maximum size of an UNDO tablespace in MB (If an UNDO tablespace grows beyond this size it will be truncated in due course).

innodb_monitor_reset_all.desc: Reset all values for a monitor counter

innodb_old_blocks_pct.desc: Percentage of the buffer pool to reserve for 'old' blocks.

innodb_old_blocks_time.desc: Move blocks to the 'new' end of the buffer pool if the first access was at least this many milliseconds ago. The timeout is disabled if 0.

innodb_online_alter_log_max_size.desc: Maximum modification log file size for online index creation

innodb_open_files.desc: How many files at the maximum InnoDB keeps open at the same time.

innodb_optimize_fulltext_only.desc: Only optimize the Fulltext index of the table

innodb_page_cleaners.desc: Page cleaner threads can be from 1 to 64. Default is number of buffer pool instances.

innodb_page_size.desc: Page size to use for all InnoDB tablespaces.

innodb_parallel_read_threads.desc: Number of threads to do parallel read.

innodb_print_all_deadlocks.desc: Print all deadlocks to MySQL error log (off by default)

innodb_print_ddl_logs.desc: Print all DDl logs to MySQL error log (off by default)

innodb_purge_batch_size.desc: Number of UNDO log pages to purge in one batch from the history list.

innodb_purge_rseg_truncate_frequency.desc: Dictates rate at which UNDO records are purged. Value N means purge rollback segment(s) on every Nth iteration of purge invocation

innodb_purge_threads.desc: Purge threads can be from 1 to 32. Default is 1 if number of available CPUs is 16 or less, 4 otherwise.

innodb_random_read_ahead.desc: Whether to use read ahead for random access within an extent.

innodb_read_ahead_threshold.desc: Number of pages that must be accessed sequentially for InnoDB to trigger a readahead.

innodb_read_io_threads.desc: Number of background read I/O threads in InnoDB.

innodb_read_only.desc: Start InnoDB in read only mode (off by default)

innodb_redo_log_archive_dirs.desc: Limit the location of the redo log archive to the semicolon separated list of labeled directories

innodb_redo_log_capacity.desc: Limitation for total size of redo log files on disk (expressed in bytes).

innodb_redo_log_encrypt.desc: Enable or disable Encryption of REDO tablespace.

innodb_replication_delay.desc: Replication thread delay (ms) on the slave server if innodb_thread_concurrency is reached (0 by default)

innodb_rollback_on_timeout.desc: Roll back the complete transaction on lock wait timeout, for 4.x compatibility (disabled by default)

innodb_rollback_segments.desc: Number of rollback segments per tablespace. This applies to the system tablespace, the temporary tablespace & any undo tablespace.

innodb_segment_reserve_factor.desc: The segment_reserve_factor is the ratio x/y expressed in percentage, where x is the number of free pages in the segment, and y is the total number of pages in the segment.  The number of used pages in the segment is given by (y-x). The number of free pages in the segment (x) will be maintained such that the actual segment_reserve_factor will be >= the requested segment_reserve_factor, which is contained in this variable.

innodb_sort_buffer_size.desc: Memory buffer size for index creation

innodb_spin_wait_delay.desc: Maximum delay between polling for a spin lock (6 by default)

innodb_spin_wait_pause_multiplier.desc: Controls how many times in a row to use a PAUSE instruction to achieve one unit of delay in a spin lock (see @@innodb_spin_wait_delay), defaults to 50

innodb_stats_auto_recalc.desc: InnoDB automatic recalculation of persistent statistics enabled for all tables unless overridden at table level (automatic recalculation is only done when InnoDB decides that the table has changed too much and needs a new statistics) (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-stats-auto-recalc to disable.)

innodb_stats_include_delete_marked.desc: Include delete marked records when calculating persistent statistics

innodb_stats_method.desc: Specifies how InnoDB index statistics collection code should treat NULLs. Possible values are NULLS_EQUAL (default), NULLS_UNEQUAL and NULLS_IGNORED

innodb_stats_on_metadata.desc: Enable statistics gathering for metadata commands such as SHOW TABLE STATUS for tables that use transient statistics (off by default)

innodb_stats_persistent.desc: InnoDB persistent statistics enabled for all tables unless overridden at table level (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-stats-persistent to disable.)

innodb_stats_persistent_sample_pages.desc: The number of leaf index pages to sample when calculating persistent statistics (by ANALYZE, default 20)

innodb_stats_transient_sample_pages.desc: The number of leaf index pages to sample when calculating transient statistics (if persistent statistics are not used, default 8)

innodb_status_file.desc: Enable SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS output in the innodb_status.<pid> file

innodb_status_output.desc: Enable InnoDB monitor output to the error log.

innodb_status_output_locks.desc: Enable InnoDB lock monitor output to the error log. Requires innodb_status_output=ON.

innodb_strict_mode.desc: Use strict mode when evaluating create options. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-strict-mode to disable.)

innodb_sync_array_size.desc: Size of the mutex/lock wait array.

innodb_sync_spin_loops.desc: Count of spin-loop rounds in InnoDB mutexes (30 by default)

innodb_table_locks.desc: Enable InnoDB locking in LOCK TABLES (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-table-locks to disable.)

innodb_temp_data_file_path.desc: Path to files and their sizes making temp-tablespace.

innodb_temp_tablespaces_dir.desc: Directory where temp tablespace files live, this path can be absolute.

innodb_thread_concurrency.desc: Helps in performance tuning in heavily concurrent environments. Sets the maximum number of threads allowed inside InnoDB. Value 0 will disable the thread throttling.

innodb_thread_sleep_delay.desc: Time of innodb thread sleeping before joining InnoDB queue (usec). Value 0 disable a sleep

innodb_undo_directory.desc: Directory where undo tablespace files live, this path can be absolute.

innodb_undo_log_encrypt.desc: Enable or disable Encrypt of UNDO tablespace.

innodb_undo_log_truncate.desc: Enable or Disable Truncate of UNDO tablespace. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-undo-log-truncate to disable.)

innodb_undo_tablespaces.deprecated: Marked deprecated in the server option help text.
innodb_undo_tablespaces.desc: Number of undo tablespaces to use. (deprecated)

innodb_use_fdatasync.desc: Use fdatasync() instead of the default fsync(). (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-use-fdatasync to disable.)

innodb_use_native_aio.desc: Use native AIO if supported on this platform. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-use-native-aio to disable.)

innodb_validate_tablespace_paths.desc: Enable validation of tablespace paths against the DD. (enabled by default). Disable with --skip-innodb-validate-tablespace-paths. (Defaults to on; use --skip-innodb-validate-tablespace-paths to disable.)

innodb_write_io_threads.desc: Number of background write I/O threads in InnoDB.

interactive_timeout.desc: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on an interactive connection before closing it

internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine.desc: The default storage engine for in-memory internal temporary tables.

join_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer that is used for full joins

keep_files_on_create.desc: Don't overwrite stale .MYD and .MYI even if no directory is specified

key_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer used for index blocks for MyISAM tables. Increase this to get better index handling (for all reads and multiple writes) to as much as you can afford

key_cache_age_threshold.desc: This characterizes the number of hits a hot block has to be untouched until it is considered aged enough to be downgraded to a warm block. This specifies the percentage ratio of that number of hits to the total number of blocks in key cache

key_cache_block_size.desc: The default size of key cache blocks

key_cache_division_limit.desc: The minimum percentage of warm blocks in key cache

keyring_migration_destination.desc: Keyring plugin or component to which the keys are migrated to.

keyring_migration_from_component.desc: Migrate from keyring component to keyring plugin.

keyring_migration_port.desc: Port number to use for connection.

keyring_migration_socket.desc: The socket file to use for connection.

keyring_migration_source.desc: Keyring plugin from where the keys needs to be migrated to. This option must be specified along with --keyring-migration-destination.

keyring_migration_to_component.desc: Migrate from keyring plugin to keyring component.

lc_messages.desc: Set the language used for the error messages.

lc_time_names.desc: Set the language used for the month names and the days of the week.

lock_wait_timeout.desc: Timeout in seconds to wait for a lock before returning an error.

log_bin.desc: Configures the name prefix to use for binary log files. If the --log-bin option is not supplied, the name prefix defaults to "binlog". If the --log-bin option is supplied without argument, the name prefix defaults to "HOSTNAME-bin", where HOSTNAME is the machine's hostname. To set a different name prefix for binary log files, use --log-bin=name. To disable binary logging, use the --skip-log-bin or --disable-log-bin option.

log_bin_index.desc: File that holds the names for binary log files.

log_bin_trust_function_creators.deprecated: '@@log_bin_trust_function_creators' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
log_bin_trust_function_creators.desc: If set to FALSE (the default), then when --log-bin is used, creation of a stored function (or trigger) is allowed only to users having the SUPER privilege and only if this stored function (trigger) may not break binary logging. Note that if ALL connections to this server ALWAYS use row-based binary logging, the security issues do not exist and the binary logging cannot break, so you can safely set this to TRUE. This variable is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

log_error_services.desc: Services that should be called when an error event is received

log_error_suppression_list.desc: Comma-separated list of error-codes. Error messages corresponding to these codes will not be included in the error log. Only events with a severity of Warning or Information can be suppressed; events with System or Error severity will always be included. Requires the filter 'log_filter_internal' to be set in @@global.log_error_services, which is the default.

log_error_verbosity.desc: How detailed the error log should be. 1, log errors only. 2, log errors and warnings. 3, log errors, warnings, and notes. Messages sent to the client are unaffected by this setting.

log_isam.desc: Log all MyISAM changes to file.

log_output.desc: Syntax: log-output=value[,value...], where "value" could be TABLE, FILE or NONE

log_queries_not_using_indexes.desc: Log queries that are executed without benefit of any index to the slow log if it is open

log_raw.desc: Log to general log before any rewriting of the query. For use in debugging, not production as sensitive information may be logged.

log_replica_updates.desc: If enabled, the replication applier threads will write to this server's binary log. (Defaults to on; use --skip-log-replica-updates to disable.)

log_short_format.desc: Don't log extra information to update and slow-query logs.

log_slave_updates.deprecated: '@@log_slave_updates' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please use log_replica_updates instead.
log_slave_updates.desc: This option is deprecated. Use log_replica_updates instead. (Defaults to on; use --skip-log-slave-updates to disable.)

log_slow_admin_statements.desc: Log slow OPTIMIZE, ANALYZE, ALTER and other administrative statements to the slow log if it is open.

log_slow_extra.desc: Print more attributes to the slow query log file. Has no effect on logging to table.

log_slow_replica_statements.desc: Log slow statements executed by the replication applier threads to the slow log if it is open.

log_slow_slave_statements.deprecated: '@@log_slow_slave_statements' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please use log_slow_replica_statements instead.
log_slow_slave_statements.desc: This option is deprecated. Use log_slow_replica_statements instead.

log_statements_unsafe_for_binlog.deprecated: '@@log_statements_unsafe_for_binlog' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
log_statements_unsafe_for_binlog.desc: Log statements considered unsafe when using statement based binary logging. This variable is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. (Defaults to on; use --skip-log-statements-unsafe-for-binlog to disable.)

log_tc.desc: Path to transaction coordinator log (used for transactions that affect more than one storage engine, when binary log is disabled).

log_throttle_queries_not_using_indexes.desc: Log at most this many 'not using index' warnings per minute to the slow log. Any further warnings will be condensed into a single summary line. A value of 0 disables throttling. Option has no effect unless --log_queries_not_using_indexes is set.

log_timestamps.desc: UTC to timestamp log files in zulu time, for more concise timestamps and easier correlation of logs from servers from multiple time zones, or SYSTEM to use the system's local time. This affects only log files, not log tables, as the timestamp columns of the latter can be converted at will.

long_query_time.desc: Log all queries that have taken more than long_query_time seconds to execute to file. The argument will be treated as a decimal value with microsecond precision

low_priority_updates.desc: INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE has lower priority than selects

lower_case_table_names.desc: If set to 1 table names are stored in lowercase on disk and table names will be case-insensitive.  Should be set to 2 if you are using a case insensitive file system

mandatory_roles.desc: All the specified roles are always considered granted to every user and they can't be revoked. Mandatory roles still require activation unless they are made into default roles. The granted roles will not be visible in the mysql.role_edges table.

master_retry_count.deprecated: Marked deprecated in the server option help text.
master_retry_count.desc: The number of times this replica will attempt to connect to a source before giving up. This option is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Use 'CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE TO SOURCE_RETRY_COUNT = <num>' instead.

master_verify_checksum.deprecated: '@@master_verify_checksum' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Please use source_verify_checksum instead.
master_verify_checksum.desc: This option is deprecated. Use source_verify_checksum instead.

max_allowed_packet.desc: Max packet length to send to or receive from the server

max_binlog_cache_size.desc: Sets the total size of the transactional cache

max_binlog_dump_events.desc: Option used by mysql-test for debugging and testing of replication.

max_binlog_size.desc: Binary log will be rotated automatically when the size exceeds this value. Will also apply to relay logs if max_relay_log_size is 0

max_binlog_stmt_cache_size.desc: Sets the total size of the statement cache

max_connect_errors.desc: If there is more than this number of interrupted connections from a host this host will be blocked from further connections

max_connections.desc: The number of simultaneous clients allowed

max_delayed_threads.deprecated: '@@max_delayed_threads' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
max_delayed_threads.desc: Don't start more than this number of threads to handle INSERT DELAYED statements. If set to zero INSERT DELAYED will be not used. This variable is deprecated along with INSERT DELAYED.

max_digest_length.desc: Maximum length considered for digest text.

max_error_count.desc: Max number of errors/warnings to store for a statement

max_execution_time.desc: Kill SELECT statement that takes over the specified number of milliseconds

max_heap_table_size.desc: Don't allow creation of heap tables bigger than this

max_insert_delayed_threads.deprecated: '@@max_insert_delayed_threads' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

max_join_size.desc: Joins that are probably going to read more than max_join_size records return an error

max_length_for_sort_data.deprecated: '@@max_length_for_sort_data' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
max_length_for_sort_data.desc: This variable is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

max_points_in_geometry.desc: Maximum number of points in a geometry

max_prepared_stmt_count.desc: Maximum number of prepared statements in the server

max_relay_log_size.desc: If non-zero: relay log will be rotated automatically when the size exceeds this value; if zero: when the size exceeds max_binlog_size

max_seeks_for_key.desc: Limit assumed max number of seeks when looking up rows based on a key

max_sort_length.desc: The number of bytes to use when sorting long values with PAD SPACE collations (only the first max_sort_length bytes of each value are used; the rest are ignored)

max_user_connections.desc: The maximum number of active connections for a single user (0 = no limit)

max_write_lock_count.desc: After this many write locks, allow some read locks to run in between

min_examined_row_limit.desc: Don't write queries to slow log that examine fewer rows than that

myisam_block_size.desc: Block size to be used for MyISAM index pages

myisam_data_pointer_size.desc: Default pointer size to be used for MyISAM tables

myisam_max_sort_file_size.desc: Don't use the fast sort index method to created index if the temporary file would get bigger than this

myisam_mmap_size.desc: Restricts the total memory used for memory mapping of MySQL tables

myisam_recover_options.desc: Syntax: myisam-recover-options[=option[,option...]], where option can be DEFAULT, BACKUP, FORCE, QUICK, or OFF

myisam_sort_buffer_size.desc: The buffer that is allocated when sorting the index when doing a REPAIR or when creating indexes with CREATE INDEX or ALTER TABLE

myisam_stats_method.desc: Specifies how MyISAM index statistics collection code should treat NULLs. Possible values of name are NULLS_UNEQUAL (default behavior for 4.1 and later), NULLS_EQUAL (emulate 4.0 behavior), and NULLS_IGNORED

myisam_use_mmap.desc: Use memory mapping for reading and writing MyISAM tables

mysql_native_password.desc: Enable or disable mysql_native_password plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

mysql_native_password_proxy_users.desc: If set to FALSE (the default), then the mysql_native_password plugin will not signal for authenticated users to be checked for mapping to proxy users.  When set to TRUE, the plugin will flag associated authenticated accounts to be mapped to proxy users when the server option check_proxy_users is enabled.

mysqlx.desc: Enable or disable mysqlx plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

mysqlx_bind_address.desc: Address to which X Plugin should bind the TCP socket optionally followed by a network namespace delimited with /. E.g., the string value 127.0.0.1/red specifies to listen on IP address 127.0.0.1 from the network namespace 'red'.

mysqlx_cache_cleaner.desc: Enable or disable mysqlx_cache_cleaner plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

mysqlx_compression_algorithms.desc: Compression algorithms: where option can be DEFLATE_STREAM, LZ4_MESSAGE, ZSTD_STREAM

mysqlx_connect_timeout.desc: Maximum allowed waiting time for connection to setup a session (in seconds).

mysqlx_deflate_default_compression_level.desc: Default value of compression level for deflate algorithm

mysqlx_deflate_max_client_compression_le.desc: Max value of compression level for deflate algorithm

mysqlx_document_id_unique_prefix.desc: Unique prefix is a value assigned by InnoDB cluster to the instance, which is meant to make document id unique across all replicasets from the same cluster

mysqlx_enable_hello_notice.desc: Hello notice is a X Protocol message send by the server after connection establishment, using this variable it can be disabled (Defaults to on; use --skip-mysqlx-enable-hello-notice to disable.)

mysqlx_idle_worker_thread_timeout.desc: Time after which an idle worker thread is terminated (in seconds).

mysqlx_interactive_timeout.desc: Default value for "mysqlx_wait_timeout", when the connection is interactive. The value defines number or seconds that X Plugin must wait for activity on interactive connection

mysqlx_lz4_default_compression_level.desc: Default value of compression level for lz4 algorithm

mysqlx_lz4_max_client_compression_level.desc: Max value of compression level for lz4 algorithm

mysqlx_max_allowed_packet.desc: Size of largest message that client is going to handle.

mysqlx_max_connections.desc: Maximum number of concurrent X protocol connections. Actual number of connections is also affected by the general max_connections.

mysqlx_port.desc: Port on which X Plugin is going to accept incoming connections.

mysqlx_port_open_timeout.desc: How long X Plugin is going to retry binding of server socket (in case of failure)

mysqlx_read_timeout.desc: Number or seconds that X Plugin must wait for blocking read operation to complete

mysqlx_socket.desc: X Plugin's unix socket for local connection.

mysqlx_wait_timeout.desc: Number or seconds that X Plugin must wait for activity on noninteractive connection

mysqlx_write_timeout.desc: Number or seconds that X Plugin must wait for blocking write operation to complete

mysqlx_zstd_default_compression_level.desc: Default value of compression level for zstd algorithm

mysqlx_zstd_max_client_compression_level.desc: Max value of compression level for zstd algorithm

ndb_allow_copying_alter_table.desc: Specifies if implicit copying alter table is allowed. Can be overridden by using ALGORITHM=COPY in the alter table command. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-allow-copying-alter-table to disable.)

ndb_applier_allow_skip_epoch.desc: Should replication applier be allowed to skip epochs

ndb_applier_conflict_role.desc: Role for applier to play in asymmetric conflict algorithms.

ndb_autoincrement_prefetch_sz.desc: Specify number of autoincrement values that are prefetched.

ndb_blob_read_batch_bytes.desc: Specifies the bytesize large Blob reads should be batched into.  0 == No limit.

ndb_blob_write_batch_bytes.desc: Specifies the bytesize large Blob writes should be batched into.  0 == No limit.

ndb_clear_apply_status.desc: Whether RESET REPLICA will clear all entries in ndb_apply_status (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-clear-apply-status to disable.)

ndb_cluster_connection_pool.desc: Pool of cluster connections to be used by mysql server.

ndb_cluster_connection_pool_nodeids.desc: Comma separated list of nodeids to use for the cluster connection pool. Overrides node id specified in --ndb-connectstring. First nodeid must be equal to --ndb-nodeid(if specified).

ndb_data_node_neighbour.desc: My closest data node, if 0 no closest neighbour, used to select an appropriate data node to contact to run a transaction at.

ndb_default_column_format.desc: Change COLUMN_FORMAT default value (fixed or dynamic) for backward compatibility. Also affects the default value of ROW_FORMAT.

ndb_deferred_constraints.desc: Specified that constraints should be checked deferred (when supported)

ndb_distribution.desc: Default distribution for new tables in NDB

ndb_eventbuffer_free_percent.desc: Percentage of free memory that should be available in event buffer before resuming buffering after the max_alloc limit is hit.

ndb_eventbuffer_max_alloc.desc: Maximum amount of memory (in bytes) that can be allocated for buffering events by the NdbApi.

ndb_extra_logging.desc: Turn on more logging in the error log.

ndb_force_send.desc: Force send of buffers to ndb immediately without waiting for other threads. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-force-send to disable.)

ndb_fully_replicated.desc: Create tables that are fully replicated by default. This enables reading from any data node when using ReadCommitted. This is great for read scalability but hampers write scalability

ndb_index_stat_enable.desc: Use ndb index statistics in query optimization. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-index-stat-enable to disable.)

ndb_index_stat_option.desc: Comma-separated tunable options for ndb index statistics

ndb_join_pushdown.desc: Enable pushing down of join to datanodes (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-join-pushdown to disable.)

ndb_log_apply_status.desc: Log ndb_apply_status updates from Master in the Binlog

ndb_log_bin.desc: Log NDB tables in the binary log. Option only has meaning if the binary log has been turned on for the server.

ndb_log_binlog_index.desc: Insert mapping between epochs and binlog positions into the ndb_binlog_index table. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-log-binlog-index to disable.)

ndb_log_cache_size.desc: Size of the binary log transaction cache used by NDB binlog

ndb_log_empty_update.desc: Normally empty updates are filtered away before they are logged. However, for read tracking in conflict resolution a hidden pesudo attribute is set which will result in an empty update along with special flags set. For this to work empty updates have to be allowed.

ndb_log_exclusive_reads.desc: Log primary key reads with exclusive locks to allow conflict resolution based on read conflicts

ndb_log_fail_terminate.desc: Terminate mysqld if complete logging of all found row events is not possible

ndb_log_orig.desc: Log originating server id and epoch in ndb_binlog_index. Each epoch may in this case have multiple rows in ndb_binlog_index, one for each originating epoch.

ndb_log_purge_rate.desc: Rate of rows to delete when purging rows from ndb_binlog_index.

ndb_log_transaction_compression_level_zs.desc: Compression level for ZSTD transaction compression in the NDB Binlog.

ndb_log_transaction_dependency.desc: Enable transaction dependency extraction for NDB changes written to the binlog.

ndb_log_transaction_id.desc: Log Ndb transaction identities per row in the Binlog

ndb_log_update_as_write.desc: For efficiency log only after image as a write event. Ignore before image. This may cause compatibility problems if replicating to other storage engines than ndbcluster. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-log-update-as-write to disable.)

ndb_log_update_minimal.desc: For efficiency, log updates in a minimal formatLog only the primary key value(s) in the before image. Log only the changed columns in the after image. This may cause compatibility problems if replicating to other storage engines than ndbcluster.

ndb_log_updated_only.desc: For efficiency log only updated columns. Columns are considered as "updated" even if they are updated with the same value. This may cause compatibility problems if replicating to other storage engines than ndbcluster. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-log-updated-only to disable.)

ndb_metadata_check.desc: Enable the automatic detection of NDB metadata changes to be synchronized with the DD (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-metadata-check to disable.)

ndb_metadata_check_interval.desc: Interval of time (in seconds) at which a check is done to see if there are NDB metadata changes to be synchronized

ndb_metadata_sync.desc: Triggers immediate synchronization of all changes between NDB Dictionary and MySQL server. Setting this option results in the values of ndb_metadata_check and ndb_metadata_check_interval being ignored. Automatically resets to false when the synchronization has completed

ndb_nodeid.desc: Set nodeid for this node. Overrides node id specified in --ndb-connectstring.

ndb_optimization_delay.desc: For optimize table, specifies the delay in milliseconds for each batch of rows sent.

ndb_optimized_node_selection.desc: Select nodes for transactions in a more optimal way.

ndb_read_backup.desc: Create tables with Read Backup flag set. Enables those tables to be read from backup replicas as well as from primary replicas. Delays commit acknowledge of write transactions to accomplish this. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-read-backup to disable.)

ndb_recv_thread_activation_threshold.desc: Activation threshold when receive thread takes over the polling of the cluster connection (measured in concurrently active threads)

ndb_replica_batch_size.desc: Batch size in bytes for the replica applier.

ndb_replica_blob_write_batch_bytes.desc: Specifies the byte size of batched blob writes for the replica applier. 0 == No limit.

ndb_report_thresh_binlog_epoch_slip.desc: Threshold for Binlog injector thread consumption lag, before reporting the Event buffer status' message with reason BUFFERED_EPOCHS_OVER_THRESHOLD. The lag is defined as the number of epochs completely buffered in the event buffer, but not consumed by the Binlog injector thread yet.

ndb_report_thresh_binlog_mem_usage.desc: Threshold on percentage of free memory before reporting binlog status. E.g. 10 means that if amount of available memory for receiving binlog data from the storage nodes goes below 10%, a status message will be sent to the cluster log.

ndb_row_checksum.desc: Create tables with a row checksum, this checks for HW issues at theexpense of performance

ndb_schema_dist_lock_wait_timeout.desc: Time (in seconds) during schema distribution to wait for a lock before returning an error. This setting allows avoiding that the binlog injector thread waits too long while handling schema operations.

ndb_schema_dist_timeout.desc: Controls how many seconds it takes before timeout is detected during schema distribution. Timeout might indicate that activity on the other MySQL Server(s) are high or are somehow prevented from acquiring the necessary resources at this time.

ndb_schema_dist_upgrade_allowed.desc: Allow schema distribution table upgrade when connecting to NDB. Use this variable to defer this change until all MySQL Servers connected to the cluster have been upgrade to same version. NOTE! The schema distribution functionality might be slightly degraded until the change has been performed. (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-schema-dist-upgrade-allowed to disable.)

ndb_show_foreign_key_mock_tables.desc: Show the mock tables which is used to support foreign_key_checks= 0. Extra info warnings are shown when creating and dropping the tables. The real table name is show in SHOW CREATE TABLE

ndb_slave_conflict_role.deprecated: Marked deprecated in the server option help text.
ndb_slave_conflict_role.desc: Role for applier to play in asymmetric conflict algorithms. This variable is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Use ndb_applier_conflict_role instead

ndb_tls_search_path.desc: Directory containing NDB Cluster TLS Private Keys

ndb_transid_mysql_connection_map.desc: Enable or disable ndb_transid_mysql_connection_map plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

ndb_use_copying_alter_table.desc: Force ndbcluster to always copy tables at alter table (should only be used if online alter table fails).

ndb_use_exact_count.desc: Use exact records count during query planning and for fast select count(*), disable for faster queries.

ndb_use_transactions.desc: Use transactions for large inserts, if enabled then large inserts will be split into several smaller transactions (Defaults to on; use --skip-ndb-use-transactions to disable.)

ndb_wait_connected.desc: Time (in seconds) to wait for connection to cluster.

ndb_wait_setup.desc: Time (in seconds) to wait for setup to complete (0 = no wait)

ndbcluster.desc: Enable or disable ndbcluster plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

ndbinfo.desc: Enable or disable ndbinfo plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

ndbinfo_max_bytes.desc: Specify approx. max number of bytes to fetch per roundtrip to cluster

ndbinfo_max_rows.desc: Specify max number of rows to fetch per roundtrip to cluster

ndbinfo_show_hidden.desc: Control if tables should be visible or not

net_buffer_length.desc: Buffer length for TCP/IP and socket communication

net_read_timeout.desc: Number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read

net_retry_count.desc: If a read on a communication port is interrupted, retry this many times before giving up

net_write_timeout.desc: Number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write

ngram.desc: Enable or disable ngram plugin. Possible values are ON, OFF, FORCE (don't start if the plugin fails to load).

ngram_token_size.desc: InnoDB ngram full text plugin parser token size in characters

offline_mode.desc: Make the server into offline mode

open_files_limit.desc: If this is not 0, then mysqld will use this value to reserve file descriptors to use with setrlimit(). If this value is 0 then mysqld will reserve max_connections*5 or max_connections + table_open_cache*2 (whichever is larger) number of file descriptors

optimizer_max_subgraph_pairs.desc: Maximum depth of subgraph pairs a query can have before the hypergraph join optimizer starts reducing the search space heuristically. Larger values may result in better query plans for large queries, but also more time and memory spent during planning. Increasing this larger than the actual number of subgraph pairs in the query will have no further effect. Ignored by the old (non-hypergraph) join optimizer

optimizer_prune_level.desc: Controls the heuristic(s) applied during query optimization to prune less-promising partial plans from the optimizer search space. Meaning: 0 - do not apply any heuristic, thus perform exhaustive search; 1 - prune plans based on number of retrieved rows

optimizer_search_depth.desc: Maximum depth of search performed by the query optimizer. Values larger than the number of relations in a query result in better query plans, but take longer to compile a query. Values smaller than the number of tables in a relation result in faster optimization, but may produce very bad query plans. If set to 0, the system will automatically pick a reasonable value

optimizer_switch.desc: optimizer_switch=option=val[,option=val...], where option is one of {index_merge, index_merge_union, index_merge_sort_union, index_merge_intersection, engine_condition_pushdown, index_condition_pushdown, mrr, mrr_cost_based, materialization, semijoin, loosescan, firstmatch, duplicateweedout, subquery_materialization_cost_based, skip_scan, block_nested_loop, batched_key_access, use_index_extensions, condition_fanout_filter, derived_merge, hash_join, subquery_to_derived, prefer_ordering_index, derived_condition_pushdown, hash_set_operations} and val is one of {on, off, default}

optimizer_trace.desc: Controls tracing of the Optimizer: optimizer_trace=option=val[,option=val...], where option is one of {enabled, one_line} and val is one of {on, default}

optimizer_trace_features.desc: Enables/disables tracing of selected features of the Optimizer: optimizer_trace_features=option=val[,option=val...], where option is one of {greedy_search, range_optimizer, dynamic_range, repeated_subselect} and val is one of {on, off, default}

optimizer_trace_limit.desc: Maximum number of shown optimizer traces

optimizer_trace_max_mem_size.desc: Maximum allowed cumulated size of stored optimizer traces

optimizer_trace_offset.desc: Offset of first optimizer trace to show; see manual

parser_max_mem_size.desc: Maximum amount of memory available to the parser

partial_revokes.desc: Access of database objects can be restricted, even if user has global privileges granted.

password_history.desc: The number of old passwords to check in the history. Set to 0 (the default) to turn the checks off

password_require_current.desc: Current password is needed to be specified in order to change it

password_reuse_interval.desc: The minimum number of days that need to pass before a password can be reused. Set to 0 (the default) to turn the checks off

performance_schema.desc: Enable the performance schema. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema to disable.)

performance_schema_accounts_size.desc: Maximum number of instrumented user@host accounts. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_consumer_events_stage.desc: Default startup value for the events_stages_current consumer.
Default startup value for the events_stages_history consumer.
Default startup value for the events_stages_history_long consumer.

performance_schema_consumer_events_state.desc: Default startup value for the events_statements_cpu consumer.
Default startup value for the events_statements_current consumer. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema-consumer-events-statements-current to disable.)
Default startup value for the events_statements_history consumer. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema-consumer-events-statements-history to disable.)
Default startup value for the events_statements_history_long consumer.

performance_schema_consumer_events_trans.desc: Default startup value for the events_transactions_current consumer. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema-consumer-events-transactions-current to disable.)
Default startup value for the events_transactions_history consumer. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema-consumer-events-transactions-history to disable.)
Default startup value for the events_transactions_history_long consumer.

performance_schema_consumer_events_waits.desc: Default startup value for the events_waits_current consumer.
Default startup value for the events_waits_history consumer.
Default startup value for the events_waits_history_long consumer.

performance_schema_consumer_global_instr.desc: Default startup value for the global_instrumentation consumer. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema-consumer-global-instrumentation to disable.)

performance_schema_consumer_statements_d.desc: Default startup value for the statements_digest consumer. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema-consumer-statements-digest to disable.)

performance_schema_consumer_thread_instr.desc: Default startup value for the thread_instrumentation consumer. (Defaults to on; use --skip-performance-schema-consumer-thread-instrumentation to disable.)

performance_schema_digests_size.desc: Size of the statement digest. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_stages_history.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_STAGES_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STAGES_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_statements_his.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_transactions_h.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_TRANSACTIONS_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_TRANSACTIONS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_events_waits_history_.desc: Number of rows in EVENTS_WAITS_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.
Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_WAITS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_hosts_size.desc: Maximum number of instrumented hosts. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_cond_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented condition objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_digest_length.desc: Maximum length considered for digest text, when stored in performance_schema tables.

performance_schema_max_digest_sample_age.desc: The time in seconds after which a previous query sample is considered old. When the value is 0, queries are sampled once. When the value is greater than zero, queries are re sampled if the last sample is more than performance_schema_max_digest_sample_age seconds old.

performance_schema_max_file_handles.desc: Maximum number of opened instrumented files.

performance_schema_max_file_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented files. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_index_stat.desc: Maximum number of index statistics for instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_logger_classes.desc: Maximum number of logger source instruments.

performance_schema_max_memory_classes.desc: Maximum number of memory pool instruments.

performance_schema_max_metadata_locks.desc: Maximum number of metadata locks. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_meter_classes.desc: Maximum number of meter source instruments.

performance_schema_max_metric_classes.desc: Maximum number of metric source instruments.

performance_schema_max_mutex_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented MUTEX objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_prepared_statemen.desc: Maximum number of instrumented prepared statements. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_program_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented programs. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_rwlock_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented RWLOCK objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_socket_instances.desc: Maximum number of opened instrumented sockets. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_sql_text_length.desc: Maximum length of displayed sql text.

performance_schema_max_statement_stack.desc: Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_CURRENT.

performance_schema_max_table_handles.desc: Maximum number of opened instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_table_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_table_lock_stat.desc: Maximum number of lock statistics for instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_max_thread_instances.desc: Maximum number of instrumented threads. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_session_connect_attrs.desc: Size of session attribute string buffer per thread. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

performance_schema_setup_actors_size.desc: Maximum number of rows in SETUP_ACTORS. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_setup_objects_size.desc: Maximum number of rows in SETUP_OBJECTS. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

performance_schema_show_processlist.desc: Default startup value to enable SHOW PROCESSLIST in the performance schema.

performance_schema_users_size.desc: Maximum number of instrumented users. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

persist_only_admin_x509_subject.desc: The client peer certificate name required to enable setting all system variables via SET PERSIST[_ONLY]

persist_sensitive_variables_in_plaintext.desc: If set to FALSE, server will refuse to persist SENSITIVE variables in plaintext and refuse to start if encrypted part of persited file cannot be processed. (Defaults to on; use --skip-persist-sensitive-variables-in-plaintext to disable.)

persisted_globals_load.desc: When this option is enabled, config file mysqld-auto.cnf is read and applied to server, else this file is ignored even if present. (Defaults to on; use --skip-persisted-globals-load to disable.)

port.desc: Port number to use for connection or 0 to default to, my.cnf, $MYSQL_TCP_PORT, /etc/services, built-in default (3306), whatever comes first

port_open_timeout.desc: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the port to become free. (Default: No wait).

preload_buffer_size.desc: The size of the buffer that is allocated when preloading indexes

print_identified_with_as_hex.desc: SHOW CREATE USER will print the AS clause as HEX if it contains non-prinable characters

profiling.deprecated: '@@profiling' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

profiling_history_size.deprecated: '@@profiling_history_size' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

protocol_compression_algorithms.desc: List of compression algorithms supported by server. Supported values are any combination of zlib, zstd, uncompressed. Command line clients may use the --compression-algorithms flag to specify a set of algorithms, and the connection will use an algorithm supported by both client and server. It picks zlib if both client and server support it; otherwise it picks zstd if both support it; otherwise it picks uncompressed if both support it; otherwise it fails.

query_alloc_block_size.desc: Allocation block size for query parsing and execution

query_prealloc_size.deprecated: '@@query_prealloc_size' is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
query_prealloc_size.desc: Persistent buffer for query parsing and execution

range_alloc_block_size.desc: Allocation block size for storing ranges during optimization

range_optimizer_max_mem_size.desc: Maximum amount of memory used by the range optimizer to allocate predicates during range analysis. The larger the number, more memory may be consumed during range analysis. If the value is too low to completed range optimization of a query, index range scan will not be considered for this query. A value of 0 means range optimizer does not have any cap on memory.
